milestones.title: Calibrate task floors and provider eligibility
acceptance_criteria: Medium risk alone does not promote every task; task kind and validated complexity/scope/coupling/duration explain the minimum tier.
Every authorized configured Claude, Codex and Antigravity account with a capable model appears as an M2 candidate; Gemini is not reserve-only for Scheduler builds.

milestones.title: Refresh quota and allocate the full DAG by effective account
acceptance_criteria: One bounded full-DAG allocation returns one model/profile/effective-account recommendation or stable reason per task without reserving M1 capacity.
Initial planning and READY assignment use due-only quota refresh evidence; stale or failed sources remain unavailable and M1 revalidates before dispatch.

milestones.title: Explain and verify assignment outcomes
acceptance_criteria: Route projections expose model, effort, profile/account, quota freshness and stable selection/exclusion reasons.
The frozen seven-task fixture proves routing behavior using only injected quota snapshots; no provider model call or task execution occurs.

tasks.title: Derive tier floors from kind, complexity, scope, coupling and duration; stop promoting on medium risk alone
tasks.objective: Set the minimum provider tier from the task's validated PLAN classification and preserve explicit high-risk/architecture uplifts.
tasks.estimate_rationale: A cross-cutting policy edit plus focused regression cases, comparable to REQ-020 T14's 120-minute policy-and-tests slice.
acceptance_criteria: A low-complexity medium-risk task stays at the task-kind floor.
High-risk, architecture/full-system and explicitly large tasks retain their approved uplift.
The decision evidence records which classification fields established the tier.

complexity.justification: Tier derivation already centralizes in one adapter and consumes validated PLAN fields.

scope.justification: The change is confined to M2's classification-to-tier adapter and its regression cases.

duration.justification: One policy function and focused cases match an existing M2 policy task.

risk.justification: A wrong tier can waste subscription quota or under-provision a high-risk task.

coupling.justification: Candidate construction consumes this tier, so its consumer must remain synchronized.

confidence.justification: The current tier rule and its Scheduler tests were inspected directly.

tasks.title: Make every capable configured provider/account a normal M2 candidate and rank quota/verified evidence before provider baseline; keep measured latency and audit routing rules
tasks.objective: Enumerate capable routes per authorized effective account and remove the M2-only static builder preference while retaining evidence-backed ranking and audit independence.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Provider-specific candidate ranking and focused route-matrix tests are comparable to REQ-020 T14's M2 policy slice.
acceptance_criteria: Claude, Codex and Antigravity profiles are candidates when model capability, project authorization, runtime and fresh quota meet the task floor.
Gemini latency influences route ordering as measured evidence but does not hard-exclude it from Scheduler build tasks.
Aliases for the same effective account are counted once, and audit-provider independence remains intact.

complexity.justification: Candidate ranking spans model ladders, quota, evidence and account identity.

scope.justification: Only Scheduler M2 candidate generation and ordering are changed; legacy pinned launch policy stays out of scope.

duration.justification: The existing M2 policy slice includes ranking changes and focused regressions.

risk.justification: A provider ranking change can concentrate or waste limited subscription capacity.

coupling.justification: The adapter depends on shared provider catalogs and D-045 route policy.

confidence.justification: The current provider ladder, candidate list and ranking contract were inspected.

tasks.title: Add a bounded, due-only quota preflight scoped to authorized effective accounts at the Scheduler boundary

verification.value: PYTHONPATH=skill/scripts:skill/scripts/tests python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest test_scheduler_quota_preflight test_subscription_usage test_agy

tasks.objective: Refresh quota only for the project's authorized effective-account pool before M2 reads the cache, while keeping M2 cache-only.
tasks.estimate_rationale: A narrow Scheduler boundary wrapper and fake-source cases, smaller than REQ-020's M2 quota policy implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Quota refresh runs at most once per due authorized effective account through existing source readers and their timeouts.
Profiles outside the project's authorized pool are not polled; aliases are deduplicated without changing persisted quota keys.
Refresh failure preserves an unavailable/unknown result and never promotes an older percentage to fresh.
Tests inject source readers and assert no model command or provider model call is made.

complexity.justification: Existing source readers already cache usage and enforce per-source polling cadence.

scope.justification: The refresh hook is scoped to the authorized project pool at M1/M2 boundary and leaves M2 core cache-only.

duration.justification: Only one adapter boundary and fake-source regressions are added.

risk.justification: A failed read or an unauthorized profile poll could expose account usage or misstate quota availability.

coupling.justification: The Scheduler adapter invokes shared subscription and Antigravity quota readers.

confidence.justification: Both source refresh entry points and the Scheduler adapter were inspected.

tasks.title: Replace independent full-plan M2 decisions with one bounded joint account-aware route map and stable no-route reasons

verification.value: PYTHONPATH=skill/scripts:skill/scripts/tests python -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest test_scheduler_decision_contract test_scheduler_decision_integration bt_scheduler_decision.tests.test_batch

tasks.objective: Use one bounded M2 batch allocation for the complete approved DAG and retain route identity, account identity and stable no-route reasons.
tasks.estimate_rationale: A full-plan adapter integration with matching and regression cases is comparable to REQ-020 T15/T18 at 180 minutes each.
acceptance_criteria: All tasks within the declared batch bound are represented exactly once in a deterministic route map.
Selection uses one shared quota/policy snapshot and effective account identity without writing M1 reservations.
Plans over the supported bound receive an explicit stable outcome rather than a partial route map.

complexity.justification: The current path loops tasks independently while M2 batch matching is bounded and account-aware.

scope.justification: This changes the route-map allocation boundary across all tasks in one approved DAG.

duration.justification: Comparable adapter and bounded-matching work took two 180-minute REQ-020 tasks.

risk.justification: A partial or over-capacity map could mislead M1 about a route that will not be used.

coupling.justification: The adapter must preserve batch-ledger identity and M1's routing contract.

confidence.justification: The full-plan adapter, batch planner and M1 route-map contract are present in the worktree.

tasks.title: Refresh and revalidate each READY batch while retaining M1's account/route reservation authority
tasks.objective: Refresh route eligibility for each READY batch and keep M1 as the only authority that reserves and dispatches a selected route.
tasks.estimate_rationale: READY-batch adapter integration and regression coverage match the 120–180-minute M2/M1 integration tasks in REQ-020.
acceptance_criteria: A quota/profile change after initial mapping causes a fresh M2 decision for a READY task.
The exact selected profile/account is passed to M1 and M1's existing atomic reservation remains authoritative.
A failed refresh or absent route cannot start a model process.

complexity.justification: The READY path batches tasks and then records individual route decisions for M1.

scope.justification: The change remains in the existing M1 assignment boundary and does not move reservation ownership.

duration.justification: M1/M2 adapter and retry integration has 120–180-minute prior task estimates.

risk.justification: Dispatch must fail closed when the fresh route or M1 reservation is unavailable.

coupling.justification: M1 contracts, M2 batch decisions and route metadata are shared across the dispatch boundary.

confidence.justification: READY routing and M1's reservation point were inspected in the current source.

tasks.title: Project the selected model, effort, profile/effective account, quota freshness and stable reasons; document the M2-specific routing ruling
tasks.objective: Expose enough route evidence to explain selected and excluded provider/model/account options to the operator.
tasks.estimate_rationale: Projection and documentation changes are smaller than prior M2 policy or full scheduler integration tasks.
acceptance_criteria: The Scheduler view identifies model, effort, human-readable profile and opaque effective-account reference for each route.
The view distinguishes fresh quota, stale/unknown quota and stable exclusion/selection reasons.
No credentials, task prose or raw quota payload are exposed in durable logs.

complexity.justification: The existing projection already carries model and profile metadata but needs account evidence and status.

scope.justification: The UI change is a small read-only projection over M1's existing route data.

duration.justification: The work is limited to a projection, one view and a decision record.

risk.justification: Showing quota must omit credentials and raw provider responses.

coupling.justification: The view consumes M1's route projection and stable M2 decision metadata.

confidence.justification: The current route projection and task view renderer were inspected.

scope.justification: Only offline routing cases and project handoff records are updated; no live task runs.

duration.justification: The existing M2 adversarial test slice estimated 180 minutes and this reuses its fixture boundary.

risk.justification: False confidence from stale quota or a synthetic run would violate the routing acceptance.
